lines.t: All paths lead to His throne, that’s the code in the bone,
Every breath, every step, every tear gets known.
From the crib to the grave to the great White Seat,
Every knee gonna drop, every heart gonna beat.
All pain, all streets, all souls get shown,
Every road, every wound, every scar gets known.
From the gutter to the gates, from the dark to the gold,
Every story, every secret, every heart gets told.
All fear, all sin, all pride gets blown,
Every path that we walk ends up at His throne.
Girl raised where the cul-de-sac glows,
Big house, cold halls, mom’s wine still flows.
Honor-roll smile with a storm inside,
Scrolling through the gram just to feel alive.Mean girl whispers cut deep like knives,
“Too much, not enough” start to script her life.
Makeup mask on, but the hurt still bleeds,
Late night DMs for a hit of “please.”Youth group songs while she breaks at home,
Knows all the words but she feels alone.
Tried pills, tried blades in the bathroom stall,
Stared at her wrist, felt nothing at all.But the Hand she can’t see never left that place,
When she stood on the bridge, when the tears hit her face.
Thought ’bout jumpin’ just to end that ache,
Felt a pull on her heart she could not shake.On the shower floor, water ice cold,
She cried, “If You’re real, I’m losin’ my soul.”
No choir, no band, just a quiet tone,
Like, “Daughter, I see you, you’re never alone.”She wept ’til the sun started pushin’ through blinds,
Felt a weight lift off she could not define.
Same girl, same scars, but a new Backbone,
Every step from that night walked toward His throne.
All pain, all streets, all souls get shown,
Every road, every wound, every scar gets known.
From the gutter to the gates, from the dark to the gold,
Every story, every secret, every heart gets told.
Man on the west side, sirens at night,
Pop locked up, mama workin’ for life.
Firstborn son with the rent on his back,
Baby bro need shoes, food runnin’ slack.Learned math on the block with a scale and pack,
Straight-A mind in a world off track.
Funerals weekly, black suits worn thin,
Every closed casket coulda been him.One shootout, bullets tore up the street,
One passed close, felt fire by his cheek.
Back at the window in a dim one-room,
He said, “If this it, I’ma die too soon.”He thought ’bout grandma and that old church pew,
Songs ’bout a King makin’ all things new.
Dropped to his knees, words broke, not clean,
“Take this life, I’m tired of this scene.”No lightning flash, just a peace rolled in,
Like Someone bigger stepped into his sin.
Got up slow, let the block life go,
Told his crew, “I’m out,” took every blow.Now he walks those streets with a different tone,
Tellin’ young ones there they’re more than they shown.
From the cells, from the hate, from the years unknown,
Every crooked, hard step got steered to His throne.
All pain, all streets, all souls get shown,
Every road, every wound, every scar gets known.
From the gutter to the gates, from the dark to the gold,
Every story, every secret, every heart gets told.
Hands rough, skin cracked, desert-night run,
Left home broke chasin’ work and sun.
Coyotes shout, border lights sweep,
Two days walkin’, no water, no sleep.Made it through fences with dust in his lungs,
Fake name written, no papers, just hung.
Found work high up on a steel-frame site,
Concrete, rebar, sweat, and height.Foreman bark like he less than man,
He just bows low, does all he can.
Sends home pay with his calloused palms,
Missin’ his kids while he hums old psalms.One noon, steel beam snapped from the crane,
Whole crew froze in a rush of pain.
Beam dropped fast, then the chain caught tight,
He lay there shakin’, knowin’ he’d been spared twice.That night in the trailer with the bare bulb glow,
He opened up a book he half didn’t know.
Read ’bout a Kingdom with an open door,
Where the poor and the stranger ain’t tossed no more.Tears hit pages, dust turned to mud,
Heart heard mercy in the printed blood.
Said, “If You’ll have me, I’ll be Yours alone,”
And his long, weary road bent up to the throne.
All pain, all streets, all souls get shown,
Every road, every wound, every scar gets known.
From the suburbs’ hush to the sirens’ tone,
From the border-line dust to the marble stone.
All tribes, all tongues, all flesh, one zone,
Every path that we walk ends up at His throne.
Three lives, three lanes, same fire, same tone,
Same Judge in the light, same Love on the throne.
When the beat cuts off and you stand alone,
You’ll see every step was a path to His throne.
